title: Good Works and Salvation
definition: Good Works and Salvation teaches that good works do not earn salvation but necessarily flow from saving grace.
summary: Good Works and Salvation clarifies that works do not earn salvation but necessarily follow saving grace.
christFocus: Jesus Christ saves His people for a life of obedience, holiness, service, and love.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Good works are the fruit of salvation, not the root of salvation. Scripture teaches that believers are saved by grace through faith, and then created in Christ for a life of obedience.

This protects the Gospel from both pride and passivity. Works cannot earn acceptance with God, but a faith that never bears fruit is not the living faith Scripture describes.

Jesus saves His people and then trains them in righteousness. Good works display His life in them and bring glory to the Father, not credit to human effort.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many either try to earn salvation through performance or claim grace while resisting obedience. This doctrine keeps salvation free and discipleship serious.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do good works as grateful obedience, not as payment for God's love. Examine whether your life bears the fruit of faith, and teach others that grace saves freely but never leaves people unchanged.
